entries.name: Kernel SHAP
entries.definition: A model-agnostic Shapley-attribution estimator using weighted linear regression on feature-presence subsets.
entries.mechanism: Fit an additive explanation model to subset-evaluation outputs with the Shapley weighting kernel and constraints fixing the empty-subset baseline and full-input prediction; sampled subsets give an approximate estimate.
entries.locator: Section 4.1, Kernel SHAP; Theorem 2 and endpoint constraints, PDF/printed pp. 5–6
entries.identity_notes: Kernel SHAP is a specific estimator within the SHAP framework. Its Shapley kernel and constraints distinguish it from an arbitrary LIME regression surrogate.
limitations: Results depend on how missing features are evaluated and on sampling; exact Shapley recovery in the full weighted problem is not a guarantee for every finite sample or background choice.
Independence approximations do not in general reproduce a dependence-aware conditional expectation.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The SHAP paper unifies additive attribution and proposes estimators; Kernel SHAP is its regression-based, model-agnostic construction.
entries.mapping_rationale: The estimator analyzes a predictive model through feature-subset evaluations of its outputs. This direct analysis relationship does not identify the estimator with a model.

entries.name: Deep SHAP
entries.definition: A compositional approximation of neural-network Shapley attributions using component-level SHAP values and backward multipliers.
entries.mechanism: Compute attributions for supported simple network components, convert them to multipliers relative to reference expectations, and compose those multipliers backward to approximate whole-network feature attributions.
entries.locator: Section 4.2, Deep SHAP, equations 13–16 and Figure 2B, PDF/printed p. 7
entries.identity_notes: Deep SHAP adapts DeepLIFT-style propagation with component SHAP values; it is a distinct approximation method, not the general SHAP definition or a synonym for all DeepLIFT rules.
limitations: Component-wise exact values do not imply exact Shapley values for an arbitrary composite nonlinear model.
Reference/background and feature-dependence assumptions affect the approximation; no causal-importance guarantee is curated.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The SHAP framework motivates a component-based neural-network approximation, whose mathematical scope is narrower than all exact Shapley attributions.
entries.mapping_rationale: The method directly propagates attributions through artificial neural networks. The mapping relates an analysis procedure to its analyzed system, not to an equivalent architecture.

entries.name: Submodular pick LIME
entries.definition: A method selecting a budgeted set of local LIME explanations by greedily increasing weighted coverage of explanatory features.
entries.mechanism: Build an instance-by-feature explanation matrix and global feature weights, then select instances by marginal gain in the total weight of features covered by at least one selected explanation.
entries.locator: Section 4, Algorithm 2 and equations 3–4, PDF/printed pp. 5–6
entries.identity_notes: SP-LIME selects representative local explanations; it is separate from fitting each LIME surrogate and does not produce a globally faithful surrogate model.
limitations: Coverage depends on the candidate instances, local explanations, interpretable features and importance weights.
The greedy coverage objective is not a guarantee of overall model trustworthiness; cross-image feature comparability requires additional choices.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Alongside local LIME explanations, the paper proposes selecting a nonredundant explanation set under a human inspection budget.
entries.mapping_rationale: The procedure selects explanations of predictive-model behavior for inspection. This direct analysis relationship does not make the selector a model class.

entries.name: Tree SHAP
entries.title: Consistent Individualized Feature Attribution for Tree Ensembles
entries.definition: A tree-specific algorithm computing Shapley feature attributions through recursive bookkeeping of weighted feature subsets along decision paths.
entries.mechanism: The original procedure follows known-feature branches and uses node cover for missing-feature branches, while EXTEND and UNWIND operations track subset sizes and repeated split features to accumulate weighted leaf contributions.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the original tree-traversal SHAP algorithm, not the TreeExplainer software package, all its later modes, or Independent Tree SHAP.
limitations: Exact computation is relative to the specified tree-traversal subset-evaluation function; it is not an assertion of exact conditional expectations for arbitrary dependent input distributions.
Background/intervention variants and nonlinear output transforms require separate method assumptions.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper develops a tractable tree-specific attribution algorithm and interaction extensions. The record curates the base traversal mechanism, not its user-study or performance claims.
entries.mapping_rationale: The method directly explains tree-model predictions. The AIO target is described under classification, whereas the attribution method also applies to regression trees and ensembles; the link is related, not equivalence or a superclass assertion.

entries.name: Gradient-weighted class activation mapping
entries.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
entries.version: ICCV 2017, pp. 618–626, CVF open-access proceedings version
entries.definition: A convolutional-network localization method weighting activation maps by spatially averaged gradients of a selected target output.
entries.mechanism: Differentiate the target score with respect to convolutional feature maps, average gradients spatially to obtain channel weights, and apply ReLU to the weighted sum of activation maps.
entries.locator: Section 3, equations 1–2, PDF pp. 3–4 / printed pp. 620–621
entries.identity_notes: Grad-CAM computes a coarse activation-space localization map. It differs from architecture-restricted CAM and from Guided Grad-CAM's additional input-space fusion.
limitations: Map resolution follows the selected convolutional layer, and ReLU retains positive weighted contributions.
A localization map is not a proof of causal influence or universal faithfulness; evaluation claims are not curated here.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper uses target gradients to localize regions in CNN-based models across several tasks. The record preserves the algorithm without generalizing conditional evaluation results.
entries.mapping_rationale: The method analyzes convolutional artificial-neural-network activations and target gradients. This is a direct analysis relation, not architecture identity.

entries.name: Guided Grad-CAM
entries.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
entries.version: ICCV 2017, pp. 618–626, CVF open-access proceedings version
entries.definition: A visualization method combining an upsampled Grad-CAM localization map with guided-backpropagation input-space scores.
entries.mechanism: Bilinearly resize the Grad-CAM map to input-image resolution, then multiply it pointwise with the guided-backpropagation visualization.
entries.locator: Section 3, Guided Grad-CAM paragraph, PDF pp. 4–5 / printed pp. 621–622; Figure 2
entries.identity_notes: Guided Grad-CAM is a specific fusion of two visualization methods, not a synonym for Grad-CAM or guided backpropagation alone.
limitations: The output inherits dependence on the selected Grad-CAM layer and the guided-backpropagation rule.
Higher image resolution and visual appeal do not establish universal explanation fidelity or causal importance.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper combines coarse target localization with a finer input-space visualization; reported evaluation benefits remain task-specific.
entries.mapping_rationale: The fused visualization analyzes artificial-neural-network behavior through convolutional activations and backward input-space signals; it is an analysis method, not a network architecture.
